task: Olfactory transduction CERT (couples nerve-conduction + GPCR/Gs-cAMP architecture shared with dopamine/serotonin + sensory/CNS layer): (1) transduction cascade, odorant -> OR (GPCR, ~400 functional human ORs per task framing, Buck & Axel 1991) -> Golf -> adenylyl cyclase III -> cAMP -> CNG channel -> Ca2+ influx -> Ca-activated Cl- channel (ANO2) amplification; one OSN expresses one OR (monogenic/monoallelic), same-OR OSNs converge on the same glomerulus; (2) the COMBINATORIAL code (Malnic, Hirono, Sato, Buck 1999): each OR recognizes multiple odorants, each odorant activates a combination of ORs, concentration changes the recruited set. FALSIFIER: force a 'one-OR-per-odorant labeled-line' adversary to reproduce Malnic 1999's measured cross-activation and concentration-dependent recruitment; quantify CNG+Cl- amplification gain and OSN dose-response. CONTESTED, held OPEN: Bushdid et al 2014's '>1 trillion odors' claim vs Gerkin & Castro 2015 and Meister 2015's critiques of the combinatorial extrapolation. Anosmia (CNGA2 loss) must abolish transduction in the model.
confidence_tier: molecular/genomic-anchored (human OR gene family, Malnic/Godfrey/Buck 2004 PMID 14983052; mouse, Godfrey/Malnic/Buck 2004 PMID 14769939) + in-vitro/ex-vivo electrophysiology-anchored (CNG discovery, Nakamura & Gold 1987 PMID 3027574; Cl- component, Kurahashi & Yau 1993 PMID 7683113 + Lowe & Gold 1993 PMID 8232590; ANO2 heterologous expression, Stephan et al 2009 PMID 19561302) + in-vivo mouse-genetic-knockout-anchored (CNGA2, Brunet/Gold/Ngai 1996 PMID 8893025; ANO2, Billig et al 2011 PMID 21516098) + in-vivo anatomical-tracing-anchored (glomerular convergence, Vassar et al 1994 PMID 8001145 + Mombaerts et al 1996 PMID 8929536). The combinatorial-code real-data falsifier (Part 4) is ex-vivo single-cell-electrophysiology-anchored but CROSS-SPECIES (Firestein, Picco, Menini 1993 PMID 8254501: tiger salamander; the rest of the doc is mouse/human) -- disclosed, not smoothed over. The discrimination-capacity figure (Bushdid et al 2014 PMID 24653035) is human-psychophysics-anchored but GENUINELY CONTESTED by Gerkin & Castro 2015 (PMID 26151673) and Meister 2015 (PMID 26151672) -- reported open, not adjudicated.

gates_summary.bug_caught_and_fixed_this_session: part2_nonlinear_adversary_falls FAILED on first run: the initial metric compared the two ENDPOINTS of the s>=1 stimulus-sweep subset (s=1 vs s=1000), which happened to catch a minor DECLINE (ratio 11.0->9.0) in an already-peaked curve, not the actual basal-to-suprathreshold RISE. Diagnosed by printing the full ratio(s) curve: ratio=1.00 at deep sub-threshold (s=1e-3), PEAKS at ~11.0 near the threshold-crossing (s~1), then settles to a ~9.0 plateau at deep saturation (both channels maxed out, relative boost compresses). Lowe & Gold 1993's own claim is a BASAL-vs-SUPRATHRESHOLD comparison ('suprathreshold responses are boosted relative to basal transduction noise'), not an endpoint-monotonicity claim across the whole suprathreshold range. Fixed by comparing the deep-sub-threshold basal floor against the sweep's PEAK (mechanistically correct per the citation's own two named regimes) rather than two arbitrary already-suprathreshold points. Re-run: fold-change=11.0, linear-null CV=0.0 (exactly flat) -- PASS, and now measuring the intended quantity. Disclosed per this repo's own memory note (subagent-fabricated-live-check / re-check cheap assertions yourself) -- self-caught by running the code and printing intermediate values, not asserted from narrative.
